vr.look: A diorama is a small, real-looking scene. The Midwest is the Heartland: flat land and rich soil grow food for the whole country.

steps.title: Get ready
steps.html:
These are the models you will use. In VR, type the gray word in the Models search box to find each one.

@MODELS@

In VR, this page is on the Canvas tab too.

steps.title: Go in
steps.html:
🔗 First time only: connect Canvas at xr.optimaed.com. See Having trouble in VR? below.

Open the On-Demand app. Click Explore. Type Countryside in Filter environments. Click The Countryside, then Begin Solo.

steps.title: Build the farm
steps.html: Find a flat spot. Put the plow at the edge, then rows of corn and wheat. Put the cow and pig nearby, and the truck at the end, ready for the city.

steps.title: Take your photo and send it
steps.html:
Open your menu, click Library, then Camera. Move the tablet until your whole diorama fits. Click Take photo.

Click the Canvas tab and pick @CANVAS@. Click Choose from My Files, pick your photo, click Use this file, then Submit to Canvas. Look for the green Submitted tag.

🔁 Want to fix it? Take a new photo and send it again.

steps.title: Check and leave
steps.html: Press the Meta button, then click Quit. Check that your photo is in the Canvas assignment. Not there? Open Having trouble in VR?

extra.html: Line up the corn and wheat in straight rows, like a real Midwest field.

vr.full: One photo that shows the field, the animals and the truck.

studio.title: From Field to Table
studio.look: Six museum cards tell how corn from a Midwest farm gets to a family's table. The cards are mixed up. The numbered spots show the order.
studio.do: Tap the card that comes first. Then tap the card that comes next, until all six spots are full.

labels.step: Tap the step that comes next.

game.miss: Not yet. What has to happen first?
game.done: Field to table! Midwest farms feed families all over the country.

steps.name: Plow the flat field
steps.ok: Yes! First the farmer gets the soil ready.
steps.hint: Before anything grows, the soil has to be ready.

steps.name: Plant corn seeds in rows
steps.ok: Yes! Seeds go into the rich soil.
steps.hint: The soil is ready. What goes in the ground now?

steps.name: Corn grows tall all summer
steps.ok: Yes! Sun and rain help the corn grow.
steps.hint: The seeds are planted. What happens next?

steps.name: Harvest the corn
steps.ok: Yes! In fall the farmer picks the corn.
steps.hint: The corn is tall now. What does the farmer do?

steps.name: A truck or train carries it to a city
steps.ok: Yes! Trucks, trains and ships carry crops.
steps.hint: The corn is picked. How does it leave the farm?

steps.name: A family in a city eats it
steps.ok: Yes! Food from the Heartland ends up on tables.
steps.hint: What is the very last step?

frames.lead: Why is the Midwest good for farming?
frames.starter: The Midwest is good for farming because ...

studio.full: All six steps are in order, and your 2 sentences have 20 words or more.
